results.name: Bosque de Chapultepec
results.principal_activities: Walking/jogging trails, boating on the lake, visiting the botanical garden, Chapultepec Castle viewpoint
results.why_it_is_special: One of the largest urban parks in Latin America (~1,700 acres across four sections), blending forests, lakes, museums, and a castle with panoramic city views — all in the heart of the capital.

results.name: Xochimilco Floating Gardens
results.principal_activities: Trajinera boat rides through ancient canals, kayaking, visiting chinampas (floating farm islands), axolotl sanctuary
results.why_it_is_special: A UNESCO-listed network of pre-Hispanic canals and artificial islands (chinampas) — the last living remnant of the Aztec lake system, offering a unique blend of ecology, agriculture, and festive culture.

results.name: Desierto de los Leones National Park
results.principal_activities: Hiking (multiple trails from easy to hard), trail running, visiting the 17th-century Ex-Convent of the Discalced Carmelites
results.why_it_is_special: Despite its name ("Desert of the Lions"), it is a lush coniferous forest just inside the city limits — Mexico's first national park (1876 as a forest reserve), with misty trails and a beautifully preserved colonial convent.

results.name: Cumbres del Ajusco National Park
results.principal_activities: Summit hiking (Pico del Águila at ~3,930 m), ridge walks, mountain biking, rock climbing
results.why_it_is_special: The highest point within Mexico City's boundaries, offering a challenging horseshoe-ridge hike with sweeping views of the Valley of Mexico — a genuine mountain experience without leaving the city.

results.name: Los Dinamos National Park (Magdalena Contreras)
results.principal_activities: Hiking to the "Puerta del Cielo" viewpoint, river-side walks, rock climbing, mountain biking
results.why_it_is_special: A forested river canyon with waterfalls and dramatic viewpoints, popular with locals for weekend picnics and outdoor sports — remarkably wild for a park inside a megacity.

results.name: Teotihuacán Pyramids & Hot-Air Balloon Flight
results.principal_activities: Climbing the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, hot-air balloon sunrise flights, walking the Avenue of the Dead
results.why_it_is_special: One of the most important ancient cities in the Americas and a UNESCO World Heritage Site; a balloon flight at sunrise over the pyramids is consistently rated among the top experiences in all of Mexico.

results.name: Nevado de Toluca (Xinantécatl)
results.principal_activities: Hiking to the crater lakes (Sol and Luna), summit attempt (4,680 m), photography
results.why_it_is_special: An extinct volcano with two stunning turquoise crater lakes set in an alpine landscape; snow-dusted in winter, it offers a dramatic high-altitude day hike accessible from the capital.

results.name: Valle de Bravo
results.principal_activities: Paragliding, sailing, kayaking, waterfall hikes, mountain biking
results.why_it_is_special: A picturesque colonial town on a large reservoir surrounded by pine-covered mountains; a beloved weekend escape from the capital with world-class paragliding and, in winter (Nov–Mar), a nearby monarch butterfly sanctuary.

results.name: Grutas de Tolantongo
results.principal_activities: Soaking in thermal river pools and cliff-side infinity pools, cave exploration, hiking canyon trails
results.why_it_is_special: A dramatic canyon with naturally heated turquoise pools cascading down the cliff face and a river-cave grotto — an other-worldly landscape that has become one of Mexico's most iconic nature destinations.

results.name: Tepoztlán & El Tepozteco
results.principal_activities: Hiking to the hilltop Aztec pyramid of El Tepozteco, browsing the weekend market, mezcal tasting
results.why_it_is_special: A charming "Magic Town" nestled beneath dramatic cliffs; the short but steep hike to the pre-Hispanic temple rewards with panoramic valley views, and the vibrant weekend market adds a cultural layer to the outing.
